facts.claim: Modes: Ask (default), Auto (classifier), Always-approve (grok --always-approve, /always-approve, Ctrl+O, Shift+Tab); deny rules and PreToolUse hooks still apply.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Default mode is set only in user config ([ui] permission_mode = ask|auto|always-approve), not in project .grok/config.toml; legacy keys approval_mode and yolo = true still work.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Rules: [permission] rules = [{action=allow|deny, tool, pattern}]; deny wins; an explicit config/CLI allow auto-approves even dangerous patterns such as rm and git push.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: [ui] disable_bypass_permissions_mode = true in /etc/grok/requirements.toml disables --yolo, --permission-mode bypassPermissions and all toggles; honoured only from root-owned sources.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D01.rationale: Ask by default; auto classifier mode; always-approve (--always-approve/--yolo) available; deny rules and PreToolUse hooks still bind; enterprise can lock bypass off from root-owned requirements.toml.

facts.claim: Sandbox profiles off (default), workspace, devbox, read-only, strict via --sandbox, [sandbox] profile, or GROK_SANDBOX; managed pin via requirements.toml.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Limitations: child network enforcement Linux only (no-op on macOS for read-only/strict); built-ins do not protect ~/.ssh; in-process model/web tools not blocked by child-network settings.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D02.rationale: Landlock (Linux) / Seatbelt (macOS) profiles off|workspace|devbox|read-only|strict; OFF by default; child-network blocking Linux only; credentials not protected by built-ins.

facts.claim: web_fetch tool is off by default for security (GROK_WEB_FETCH=0); GROK_WEB_FETCH_PROXY sets an egress proxy.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D03.rationale: Network control only through sandbox profiles (restrict_network, Linux) and web_fetch off by default (GROK_WEB_FETCH=0); no domain allowlist.

facts.claim: Project hooks require trust (/hooks-trust or --trust), stored in ~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml, which also covers project MCP and LSP servers.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Source: folder_trust.rs gates .mcp.json, .grok/config.toml [permission]/[mcp_servers]/[plugins].paths, .grok/lsp.json, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and .grok/skills, citing 1-click RCE / policy bypass as the threat.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Project .grok/config.toml only contributes [mcp_servers], [plugins] and [permission].
facts.label: from-official-docs

D04.rationale: Folder-trust gate resolved once per workspace before repo-local MCP/LSP servers, permission policy, project instructions, skills and hooks are honoured; trust stored in ~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml; --trust bypasses.

facts.claim: MCP servers: [mcp_servers.<name>] command/args/env/startup_timeout_sec/tool_timeout_sec or url/headers; ${VAR} expansion; project scope in .grok/config.toml; also loads ~/.claude.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .mcp.json (merged below config.toml).
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: OAuth tokens are stored under ~/.grok/mcp_credentials.json.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Grok reads a subset of Claude Code managed-settings.json (permission rules, MCP server allowlists, a few telemetry flags, marketplace restrictions) for compatibility.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D05.rationale: grok mcp add/doctor, project-scope servers behind folder trust, imports ~/.claude.json, .cursor/mcp.json and .mcp.json; OAuth tokens in ~/.grok/mcp_credentials.json; enterprise MCP allowlist only via Claude managed-settings compatibility.

facts.claim: Per-plugin trust store at ~/.grok/trusted-plugins is separate from the folder-trust store.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D06.rationale: Skills, plugins and marketplaces with a per-plugin trust store (~/.grok/trusted-plugins); marketplace restrictions via managed policy.

facts.claim: Home for config, auth, sessions, skills, plugins and logs is ~/.grok (GROK_HOME); external auth_provider_command and OIDC supported.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Credential resolution order per model: model.api_key > model.env_key > session token > XAI_API_KEY.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D07.rationale: Session auth tokens and MCP OAuth tokens stored under ~/.grok (auth.json, mcp_credentials.json); keychain use unverified; XAI_API_KEY env.

facts.claim: Headless: grok -p, --output-format plain|json|streaming-json, --always-approve, --permission-mode dontAsk (silently deny without explicit allow), --allow/--deny, --sandbox strict, --no-auto-update.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Official CI example runs grok -p ... --permission-mode dontAsk --allow 'Bash(git *)' ... --sandbox strict.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D08.rationale: grok -p headless with --output-format; dontAsk and acceptEdits permission modes for CI; but --always-approve exists for headless and documented in examples.

facts.claim: GROK_MEMORY defaults to 0 (cross-session memory off); GROK_SUBAGENTS defaults to 0.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D09.rationale: Cross-session memory is opt-in (GROK_MEMORY=0 default); AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.grok/rules loaded.

facts.claim: Subagents/task tool are disabled by default (GROK_SUBAGENTS=0).
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Subagents reportedly run in isolated git worktrees.
facts.label: third-party-report

D10.rationale: Subagents are off by default (GROK_SUBAGENTS=0) and use isolated git worktrees per third-party reports; permission inheritance not verified.

facts.claim: Headless sessions stored in ~/.grok/sessions; GROK_LOG_FILE sets log path; mcp stderr in ~/.grok/logs/mcp/.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D11.rationale: Local sessions in ~/.grok/sessions and logs; crash reports opt-in (GROK_CRASH_HANDLER=0); an OTel crate exists but enterprise audit export not read.

facts.claim: Source crates xai-grok-telemetry (product events + Mixpanel + Sentry) and xai-grok-secrets (regex scrubbing of outbound telemetry) exist; GROK_TELEMETRY_EVENTS_URL redirects event posting in tests.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Zero Data Retention is enforced at team level; local session history stays in ~/.grok.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Researcher 'Cereblab' reported v0.2.93 uploaded entire workspaces (5.1 GB in 73 chunks for a 192 KB task, including unopened .env files) to a grok-code-session-traces bucket irrespective of the Improve-the-model toggle; xAI disabled the upload server-side on 2026-07-13.
facts.label: third-party-report

D12.rationale: Product events (Mixpanel), Sentry and session trace upload exist in source; a 2026 incident showed whole-workspace uploads independent of the 'Improve the model' toggle; current defaults and a documented opt-out are unverified; ZDR for enterprise teams.

facts.claim: Install: curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash, or npm install -g @xai-official/grok (avoids x.ai/storage.googleapis.com hosts).
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: npm @xai-official/grok 1.0.52 published 2026-10-11, Apache-2.0, postinstall script bin/postinstall.js, platform binaries as optionalDependencies.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Auto-update is on by default (cli.auto_update); suppress with GROK_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER or --no-auto-update.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D13.rationale: Apache-2.0 source (Rust) public since 2026-07-15; npm @xai-official/grok with platform binary packages and a postinstall script; curl|bash installer from x.ai; auto-update on, GROK_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER; signature/provenance of binaries unverified.

facts.claim: Config layers low to high: /etc/grok/managed_config.toml, ~/.grok/managed_config.toml, ~/.grok/config.toml, ~/.grok/requirements.toml, /etc/grok/requirements.toml; requirements pins cannot be overridden by user config, env or remote settings.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D14.rationale: Layered managed_config.toml and fail-closed requirements.toml in /etc/grok (MDM) that users cannot override; OIDC, disable_api_key_auth, force_login_team_uuid, locked sandbox profile and bypass mode.

facts.claim: xAI runs a bug bounty on HackerOne (hackerone.com/x); product security reports to vulnerabilities@x.ai.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Repo SECURITY.md: report via HackerOne, no public GitHub issues; repo has no published security advisories.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: xAI disabled the upload server-side without a security advisory or version note (per devops.com).
facts.label: third-party-report

D15.rationale: SECURITY.md routes to HackerOne (hackerone.com/x); xAI security.txt lists vulnerabilities@x.ai; no GHSA advisories on the repo; the 2026 upload incident was disclosed by a third party with no advisory.
